definitions.note: an adverb phrase meaning almost, matching the adverb

indicators.note: a capital letter is the first one, so the opening letter of Namibian is taken

parts.note: something at an early stage has not yet developed

explanation.surface: A comment on Windhoek as a city still waiting to grow, with an exclamation of near agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Namibian capital' looks like Windhoek, but 'capital' only asks for the first letter, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean almost or very nearly, a straight synonym pair.

clue.text: Partiality gets me in post improperly

indicators.note: words arranged improperly are put in a wrong order, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone complains that being given a job without merit shows favouritism.
explanation.definitionFit: Favouring relatives or friends in appointments is a form of bias, so partiality is a fair synonym.

indicators.note: in tells us the bird sits inside the other letters

parts.note: something last-minute is late
a tern is a seabird, so a creature with wings

explanation.surface: A football manager brings a wide player on as a late substitution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a footballer on the flank; here it is a seabird, and 'in' splits the other letters around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To switch back and forth between two things is to take turns, the verb sense.

parts.note: an apprentice is a learner, and L is the learner's plate letter
the word and joins things together, a conjunction

explanation.surface: A trainee carpenter is working at a shipyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joiner' poses as a carpenter but means a conjunction.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat that docks comes ashore, a verb synonym for arriving at the quay.

indicators.note: gripping means holding tightly, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: pains are aches
sick means ill

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek invalid is racked with pains.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to the hero's famously vulnerable heel.
explanation.definitionFit: The warrior hero of the Trojan War in Homer's Iliad is an ancient Greek figure.

parts.note: to con someone is to cheat them
to tempt is to entice or seduce

explanation.surface: A list of a cad's misdeeds: deceive, seduce, then sneer.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorn and disdain are synonyms for looking down on someone.

clue.text: One disease initially harboured by friendly cow

indicators.note: harboured by means sheltered inside, so these letters go within the other word

parts.note: intimate means close and friendly
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of disease is used

explanation.surface: A sociable cow is carrying the first signs of an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cow' looks like an animal but is the verb meaning to bully into submission.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to frighten them into obeying, a verb synonym.

parts.note: a student is a learner, abbreviated L, with the 's meaning is
to earn is to be paid for work

explanation.surface: A student realises they will be paid for their work.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to know or grasp something is a sense shared by both words.

indicators.note: acting foolishly suggests disorder, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A girlfriend unwisely goes on dates with an American.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular boyfriend or girlfriend is informally called one's steady, a noun sense.

clue.text: Exposed a scholar with Leninist sympathies

parts.note: a BA, a Bachelor of Arts, is a scholar
a communist sympathiser is a Red

explanation.surface: An academic is revealed as having communist leanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid bare means uncovered or revealed, the past participle matching.

clue.text: Favourite university — one found in Beds

definitions.note: short for a thing found in flower beds; one does double duty here

parts.note: a favourite is a pet
a means one

explanation.surface: A favourite college sits among others in Bedfordshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beds' looks like the county abbreviation for Bedfordshire, an English county; here it means flower beds.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a bedding plant commonly grown in garden flower beds.

clue.text: I natter irresponsibly in the compound

indicators.note: letters treated irresponsibly are thrown about carelessly into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to chatting carelessly inside a walled enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' suggests an enclosure; it is a chemical compound.
explanation.definitionFit: A salt of nitric acid is a chemical substance, an example of a compound.

definitions.meaning: milk that goes off becomes sour
a performer's act or routine on stage

explanation.definitionFit: Milk going sour is said to change this way, and a stage routine is a music-hall slot.

clue.text: Try to stop my old Dutch being resolute

parts.note: to deter is to try to prevent
mine is an archaic form of my, used before a vowel

explanation.surface: Someone tries to stop their wife from being stubborn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my old Dutch' is Cockney slang for one's wife, but here it splits into MINE (old form of my) and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Firmly decided and unwavering are shared senses of both words.

indicators.note: makes signals that the following letters are made into something new by rearranging

explanation.surface: A politician passes a law permitting rioting.
explanation.definitionFit: A Member of Parliament is a lawmaker, a specific example of the general term.

definitions.meaning: went up a wall or mountain
covered with scales as a reptile's skin is

explanation.definitionFit: Ascended a cliff, and having a skin of small horny plates as reptiles do.

clue.text: Quick to catch fish that's straggling

indicators.note: to catch means to hold inside, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: spry means quick and lively
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: An angler moves fast to land a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Handwriting with long thin uneven strokes is described as spindly, like a spider's legs.

clue.text: Soldier's stiffly formal and incurring censure

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, soldiers, with the 's meaning is
prim means stiffly proper

explanation.surface: A rigidly correct soldier draws a rebuke from his officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal rebuke is a censure, the noun sense.

indicators.note: accept means take in, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: to yank is to pull or drag
a win is a success

explanation.surface: Americans welcome the success of an art exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yanks' looks like Americans but is the verb, pulls.
explanation.definitionFit: Sketches in pencil or ink are pictures, examples of works of art.

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so one word holds the other

parts.note: a canon is a principle or tenet
men means people

explanation.surface: A cathedral clergyman takes in lodgers at his home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canon' suggests a clergyman; it is a rule, TENET.
explanation.definitionFit: A block of flats or rented rooms is a form of residential accommodation.

clue.text: Charged back into abstemious surroundings to make mischief

indicators.note: into, with surroundings, says one word goes inside the other
surroundings says the second word encloses the first

parts.note: an abstemious place is dry, with no alcohol

indicators.note: back means the word is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: a charged wire is live

explanation.surface: An electrified rebel crashes into a teetotal setting to cause trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LIVE into EVIL, which goes into DRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicked or playful wrongdoing is mischief, a noun synonym.

indicators.note: enters means goes into, so this letter is placed inside the word

parts.note: flat beer or bread is stale

explanation.surface: A royal moves into a plain apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an apartment but means stale.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple food or item is a fundamental one, so as an adjective it means essential.

parts.note: a staff is a body of workers

explanation.surface: Employees are posted to a Hebridean island.
explanation.definitionFit: This small Inner Hebrides island is home to Fingal's Cave.

clue.text: Not out raising support in the country

parts.note: in is the opposite of out, as a batsman still at the crease

indicators.note: raising means lifting up, which in a down clue reads the letters bottom to top

parts.note: aid is support

explanation.surface: A batsman still in play lifts up a fallen comrade abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a nation in South Asia, an example of a country.

parts.note: tiddly is British slang for slightly drunk
a wink can be a flirtatious signal

explanation.surface: A tipsy bar-goer flirts across the bar counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' suggests a bar or shop fitting; here it is a playing piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The small disc flicked into a cup in the children's game is a playing piece, a counter.

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some of the curtains were sewn domestically.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtains is slang for the end of life, as in it's curtains for him.

definitions.meaning: the American spelling of the rubber ring fitted round a wheel

explanation.definitionFit: To wear someone out, and the US spelling of a wheel's rubber covering.

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ados are fusses or commotions

explanation.surface: Someone makes a fuss about a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Fizzy water or a soft drink is a beverage.

parts.note: a flat is an apartment
ten is a number

explanation.surface: An address: apartment number, and which storey it is on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floor' looks like a storey; it is the verb, to knock down.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor an opponent is to knock them down, a verb synonym.

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
so means very, as in so good
late can mean recent, as in the late news

explanation.surface: Someone describes a single person whose split was very fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divorce' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to separate.
explanation.definitionFit: To set apart or separate something is the shared verb sense.

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone noticed that a man supported revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past of see; it is a noun, an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is a traditional saying or proverb, a maxim.

parts.note: and means with or plus

explanation.surface: A criminal is said to have a natural gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A robber living outside the law is a brigand, a synonym.
